1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
data(starwars)
library(jtools)
```


2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+ geom_bar()
```


3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc. 
```{r}
library(viridis)
starwars$eye_color<- relevel(as.factor(starwars$eye_color), ref = "unknown")
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color, fill = eye_color))+ geom_bar(color = "aquamarine", width = 0.8) + scale_fill_viridis(option = "mako", discrete = TRUE) + theme_dark() + labs(x = "Character Eye Color", y = "Count", title = "Character Eye Color Frequency") + theme(legend.position = "none")
```


4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, homeworld)) + geom_boxplot()
```


5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(homeworld, height/100, fill = homeworld)) + geom_boxplot() + labs(title = "Character Height by Homeworld", y = "height (meters)")+ theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5))

# https://www.r-bloggers.com/2024/03/rotate-ggplot2-axis-labels-in-r-improve-plot-readability/
```


6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point()
```


7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height/100, mass, color = height))+geom_point(shape = 3) + scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma")+ theme_bw() + labs(title = "Character Height vs Mass", x = "Height (meters)", y = "Weight (kg)") + theme(legend.position = "none")
```


8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height/100, mass, color = gender))+geom_point()
```


9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height/100, mass, color = gender))+geom_point() + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Character Height vs Mass Defined by Gender", x = "Height (meters)", y = "Weight (kg)")
```
